checklist.title: Can distributed blob publishing send data columns to subnets the node is NOT subscribed to?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the distributed blob publishing logic in the P2P layer (SG-010). 2. Enumerate all code paths that publish data columns to subnets. 3. For each publishing call, verify that there is a pre-check confirming the node is subscribed to the target subnet (either custody or sampling subscription). 4. Create test scenarios where: (a) node subscription state changes during publishing, (b) subnet list is empty or malformed, (c) race conditions between subscription updates and publishing. 5. Verify that no data column is ever published to a subnet where the node lacks an active subscription. 6. Check for off-by-one errors in subnet index calculations. 7. Verify custody subnet and sampling subnet subscription checks are both enforced.
checklist.falsification_approach: Attempt to trigger a state where the node publishes a data column to a subnet it is not subscribed to by: (1) rapidly changing subscription state, (2) corrupting subnet subscription list, (3) forcing edge cases in subnet index mapping.
checklist.invariant_under_test: For all published data columns D and target subnets S: publish(D, S) implies (is_custody_subscribed(S) OR is_sampling_subscribed(S))
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0043, Primary Element: p2p:SG-010:distributed_blob_publishing, Property Type: invariant

checklist.title: Verify anti-equivocation cache is unconditionally updated on data column import
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code paths where data columns are imported in the distributed_blob_publishing component (SG-010). 2. Trace each import path to verify the anti-equivocation cache update call occurs unconditionally. 3. Check for early returns, error handling branches, or conditional logic that could skip cache updates. 4. Specifically verify that publication failure (gossip publish errors) does not prevent cache updates. 5. Design test cases: (a) successful import with successful publish - verify cache updated, (b) successful import with failed publish - verify cache still updated, (c) failed import - verify appropriate cache behavior. 6. Look for race conditions where cache update could be lost due to concurrent operations. 7. Verify the cache update happens atomically with or before any state that could be observed externally.
checklist.falsification_approach: Attempt to create a scenario where data columns are successfully imported but the anti-equivocation cache is not updated. Focus on: (1) Publication failure paths - simulate gossip publish failures and verify cache is still updated. (2) Error handling paths - inject errors after import but before cache update. (3) Concurrent access - race two imports to see if cache update can be skipped. (4) Conditional branching - analyze control flow for any conditions that gate cache updates.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0044, Post-condition violation could allow equivocation attacks where an attacker publishes conflicting data columns without detection. The anti-equivocation cache is critical for preventing double-signing or conflicting blob publication attacks in the P2P layer.

checklist.title: Verify Blob Retrieval Atomicity: Does distributed blob publishing abort when engine_getBlobsV2 returns incomplete blob set?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the distributed blob publishing code path (p2p:SG-010). 2. Locate where engine_getBlobsV2 is called and responses are processed. 3. Simulate partial blob responses where engine_getBlobsV2 returns fewer blobs than expected in kzg_commitments. 4. Verify that the publishing operation aborts entirely without emitting any data columns to the P2P network. 5. Check for race conditions where partial publication could occur before the completeness check. 6. Verify error handling logs the incomplete response appropriately. 7. Confirm no partial data columns are gossiped or stored when blob retrieval is incomplete.
checklist.falsification_approach: Attempt to bypass the blob completeness pre-condition by: (1) Returning partial blob sets from engine_getBlobsV2 with valid but incomplete data. (2) Returning blobs that do not match the expected kzg_commitments. (3) Timing attacks where blobs arrive incrementally. (4) Testing edge cases: zero blobs returned, one blob missing, commitment mismatch on single blob. (5) Verify the count check correctly compares against block.kzg_commitments length.
checklist.precondition_under_test: len(engine_getBlobsV2_response.blobs) == len(block.kzg_commitments) AND all(blob.commitment == expected for blob, expected in zip(blobs, kzg_commitments))
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0046, Pre-condition: All blobs matching kzg_commitments must be retrieved before publishing data columns. Failure to enforce this atomicity could result in partial data column publication, potentially causing network inconsistency or allowing peers to infer incomplete blob data. This is a trust boundary check at the Engine API interface between consensus and execution layers.
